purpose: Make the proposition, actor, action, condition, and consequence easy to recover from the sentence.
rules: State the main proposition before commentary about the act of stating it.
Name the actor and action when known.
Prefer a direct verb over a noun phrase that hides the action.
Keep causal and temporal order explicit.
Split long dependency chains when doing so preserves relations more clearly.
Use passive voice when the actor is unknown, irrelevant, or the affected object must lead; do not use it to hide a known responsible actor.
Put material conditions next to the proposition they limit.
Use one uncertainty mechanism for one uncertainty unless two independent uncertainties actually differ.
antiPatterns: generic balanced-opposition framing without a decision or evidence distinction
